headline: Six and a half hours to the Globex restart and the CME weekend halt still governs: Stress eases two points to 80% on the first one-sided de-escalatory hour of the weekend - Kushner is reported heading into a direct meeting with Hamas leadership in Egypt and no new Hormuz, Lebanon or Saudi escalation has landed in three hours - Tail unchanged at 16%, EA_ON and green, Confidence 79%
statusText:
Nothing has traded. The CME weekend halt still sets the published state: NQ futures have not quoted since Friday 14 August and Globex does not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC tonight, about six and a half hours from this run. Tail is 16%, the action is EA_ON and the status is green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting, and the last observed path was benign.

The change this hour is direction, not magnitude. For the first time this weekend the marginal news is one-sided in the de-escalatory direction, so Stress comes down two points from 82% to 80% rather than continuing to climb.

Two entries landed since the last run. Hamas sources told AFP that Jared Kushner will meet Hamas leadership in Egypt with Egyptian and Qatari officials present, before travelling to Israel to meet Netanyahu. That is a materially bigger step than yesterday's presidential courtesy call: it is a direct channel to the party that has to implement the ceasefire, with both mediators in the room. Separately, Israel's national security minister Ben Gvir made inflammatory comments about Gaza. That is domestic political rhetoric with no transmission channel into index-level structure, and it is not scored.

What did not happen matters as much. No new Hormuz incident, no new Lebanon strike, no new Saudi or Houthi action and no new sanctions detail has appeared in roughly three hours of liveblog coverage. Meanwhile Bloomberg's analysis of the promised Bessent package - carried onward by the Japan Times this morning - concludes the remaining levers run mainly through Iran's China ties and that pressing them risks blowback on the US economy, with several analysts openly sceptical given Iran already faces a naval blockade and thousands of existing sanctions. That does not remove the catalyst, but it caps the plausible magnitude of the shock.

Last hour's assessment named the risk that Stress had ratcheted from 54% to 82% across a window in which no venue quoted once, and that part of that climb was a re-reading of a static evidence set rather than new information. This hour acts on that: an hour with genuine de-escalation and no new escalation should move Stress down, and it does. The underlying stack - an unpriced weekend, a single thin-liquidity restart, and implied volatility that closed near the bottom of its 52-week range - is unchanged, which is why the move is two points rather than ten.
recommendation:
Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 16% maps to EA_ON and green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to defend against while the venue is shut. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always.

The roughly 22:00 UTC Globex restart is the only checkpoint inside this forecast window, and the danger window stays anchored to it at 21:55-00:00 UTC, 23:55-02:00 Berlin. That is deliberately narrower than a whole-session shutdown: the risk sits in the gap itself and in the first two hours of thin Asian-transition liquidity, not across the whole session. A weekend of Gaza, Lebanon and Hormuz headlines plus a US sanctions package signposted for the coming week has to clear into a single restart against a market that closed with implied volatility near the bottom of its 52-week range.

Forecast Tail drifts 16% to 19% through the remaining halt, steps to 21% at 21:00 UTC and peaks at 26% and 25% across the first two hours of live quoting - orange, block new base entries - before easing through the watch band and returning to green at 04:00 UTC Monday. That peak is one point lower than last hour, which is the correct size of response to one de-escalatory hour: the gap risk is slightly smaller, not resolved.

This is general market-risk assessment for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice, and it is not a recommendation to place any trade.
body:
Observed reference levels, all from Friday 14 August's close because nothing has traded since, and all re-verified from primary quote pages this hour. NQU26 settled at 30,141.75, down 46.75 points or 0.15%, opening at 30,210.75 against a 30,188.50 previous close and holding a 254-point range of 30,028.50 to 30,283.00 on 397,964 contracts. Investing.com still marks the contract Closed as of 14/08. It finished mid-range, roughly 2.7% below the 52-week high of 30,975.50 and far above the 22,961.50 low. There is no persistent directional efficiency in that, no shallow-pullback extension, no repeated failed retracement and no close near an extreme - the four things the contract requires before Tail belongs above 25%.

Volatility and rates. VIX closed at 14.25, down 0.38 or 2.60%, opening 14.64 with a day range of 14.18 to 14.72 against a previous close of 14.63 and a 52-week range of 13.38 to 35.30 - near the bottom of that range but not the low of 2026. That figure was re-read directly from Yahoo Finance this hour and is stamped 14 August 15:15 CDT, confirming no update since Friday's close. The 2-year yield finished Friday at 4.171%, up 3.1bp on a 4.098 to 4.178 range, and the 10-year at 4.696%, up 5.5bp; those are carried from last hour's primary read, as no venue has repriced them. Modest bear-steepening, not a cross-asset stress impulse. Low implied volatility into an unpriced restart is a thin cushion - a Stress statement, not a Tail one.

Equities and breadth from Friday. The Nasdaq Composite closed 26,729.16, down about 0.3%; the S&P 500 eased 0.2% from its record high and the Dow fell 0.2%, while the Russell 2000 rose 0.51% to 3,068, a fresh record and its third all-time high of the week. On the week the S&P added 0.4% and the Nasdaq 0.1% while the Dow fell 0.6% - a third straight weekly gain for both the S&P and the Nasdaq. A small-cap record set on a day the Nasdaq fell is broadening, not the narrow mega-cap leadership that typically precedes a one-way index break. Semiconductors were dispersed rather than aligned, with Broadcom down 5.9% and Intel 2% against AMD up 6.5% and Micron 2.3%, and dispersion inside the complex is the opposite of the alignment that would manufacture index-level one-way structure.

Oil, re-read this hour and unchanged because the tape is shut. WTI is $82.40, up $1.15 or 1.42% on Friday, roughly 5% on the week, 3.52% on the month and 32.95% year on year; Brent $88.52. Trading Economics still attributes the weekly gain to Washington increasing economic pressure on Iran while the naval blockade of Iranian ports holds, with the IEA warning of the widest global supply deficit in five years, some tankers running without active transponders, US forces expanding vessel escort capability, and the Houthi strikes on the Jazan refinery. The one softening element in that same note is on the demand side: the IEA has lowered global consumption projections, citing prolonged conflict and elevated prices, and additional Middle Eastern barrels reaching the US may ease tight inventories. The strait has been effectively shut since late February and the Iran-Oman talks on reopening it remain stalled, with Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Rezaei publicly conditioning any reopening on the unfreezing of Iranian funds held overseas.

The hour's new information, and why it moves Stress down rather than up. Hamas sources told AFP that Kushner will meet Hamas leadership in Egypt with Egyptian and Qatari officials present, then travel to Israel to meet Netanyahu. Last hour the diplomatic track was a presidential meeting with Sisi; this hour it is a direct channel to the implementing party with both mediators at the table. Ben Gvir's remarks about Gaza are inflammatory but carry no index-level transmission mechanism and are not scored. Nothing new arrived on Hormuz, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia or the Houthis in roughly three hours of liveblog coverage, which after a weekend of steady escalation is itself informative.

The sanctions catalyst is now better characterised without being resolved. Treasury Secretary Bessent said on 13-14 August that Washington would apply measures "like have never been seen in the history of the economic isolation of a country," with details due this coming week and the Hormuz blockade maintained. Bloomberg's follow-up analysis, syndicated by the Japan Times this morning, finds the realistic remaining levers concentrated in Iran's trade and financial links with China, and notes that pressing them risks blowback on the US economy; several analysts are openly sceptical that much headroom exists given the existing blockade and thousands of standing sanctions. That is a confirmed, high-impact, unscheduled catalyst with a direct oil transmission channel and no timestamp, which is why it stays in the Stress path rather than in a second danger window - but a better-bounded catalyst is a smaller one.

Friday's macro still deserves to be carried forward. July retail sales fell 0.6%, the worst print since May 2025, and preliminary August consumer sentiment came in at 51.0 against 54.5 expected, with the dollar falling to a one-week low. Equities took this benignly because it cut perceived odds of a September Fed hike, but a weakening consumer is a real seed for a growth scare and is part of why Stress sits in the extreme band while Tail does not.

Calendar, re-verified against Trading Economics this hour. The seven-day US list is front-loaded with housing and survey data on Monday and Tuesday, FOMC Minutes on Wednesday 19 August at 18:00 UTC, jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed index on Thursday, and the S&P Global flash PMIs on Friday 21 August as the high-impact anchors. Weekly API and EIA crude stock changes and the Baker Hughes rig count are added at medium impact this hour given how much of the current risk narrative runs through oil. One honest caveat: this hour's read of the same Trading Economics page rendered the Empire State index as high impact and the weekly ADP print as medium, exactly inverting last hour's read of the same page. A single ambiguous scrape is not enough to flip a published rating in either direction, so both are left as previously published and the discrepancy is disclosed rather than silently resolved. Nothing falls on 22-23 August. Jackson Hole is 27-29 August with Kevin Warsh due to give his first keynote as Fed chair on 28 August, and Nvidia earnings land the week after next - the two largest scheduled catalysts both sit beyond this window. Walmart and other large retailers report during the coming week, relevant to the consumer question but not to Nasdaq-100 structure.

Evidence quality. Confidence 79%, up one point. The NQ future, VIX, oil, the Times of Israel liveblog and the seven-day calendar were all read directly from primary pages this hour and are mutually consistent, and the liveblog is current to roughly 14:55 UTC. The Bessent package is now corroborated across Bloomberg, the Japan Times, Middle East Eye and RFE/RL rather than a single wire, and this hour adds analytical detail on its likely shape. Two fetches failed: the CNBC week-ahead article returned HTTP 403, and the Investing.com economic calendar rendered only the current day rather than the forward week - the first was replaced from search-level reporting and the second by the Trading Economics calendar, so no input was lost. The one irreducible gap remains that no live price path exists at all. During a scheduled venue halt that absence is a certain, known fact rather than an unreliable reading, which is why it caps Confidence in the lower half of the high band rather than pushing it down.
lookbackSummary:
The trailing 24 hours run from 15:00 UTC Saturday to 14:00 UTC Sunday and sit entirely inside the CME weekend halt. Claude published in every one of those hours and the outcome was identical each time: EA_ON, green, dominantMode mixed. Tail never left the low band, drifting 10% to 16%. Stress carried all the movement, running 56, 58, 57, 60, 62, 65, 67, 67, 68, 70, 71, 73, 74, 75, then dipping to 70 and climbing 71, 71, 78, 79, easing to 78, then 80, 78, 81 and 82. Confidence rose almost monotonically from 61% to 78%.

Three features of that track matter for reading the current hour. First, the entire Stress climb from the mid-fifties to the low eighties happened across a market that never quoted once. Part of it is genuine - Saturday's south-Lebanon strikes and the Bessent package were new information - but part is a re-reading of a static evidence set as the reopen approaches. Last hour named that risk explicitly; this hour acts on it, and Stress comes down for the first time since the halt began on the first hour whose marginal news was one-sided in the de-escalatory direction.

Second, the 80-78-81-82 oscillation across the 11:00 to 14:00 slots is the honest signature of genuinely conflicting inputs rather than drift: 12:00 cut Stress on an opening diplomatic channel, 13:00 partly reversed it when two IDF strikes landed inside Gaza and the Bessent catalyst surfaced, and 14:00 added a single point on an Iranian bounty and a Jazan warning set against the Kushner-Sisi meeting. The current hour breaks that pattern because for the first time nothing escalatory arrived at all.

Third, the near-monotonic Confidence rise from 61% to 78% is genuine and continues to 79%. Successive hours added primary-source coverage of levels, volatility, rates, oil, breadth and the calendar even though the price path stayed unavailable. Tail's 10-to-16 drift across the whole window is the smallest movement in the set, which is the correct behaviour when the input that drives Tail - observed price path - has been absent for every single slot.
outlookSummary:
The next 24 hours end at 14:00 UTC Monday, so the roughly 22:00 UTC Globex restart and the first sixteen hours of live quoting sit inside the window. Tail stays in the low band for the six remaining halt slots, drifting 16% to 19%, then steps to 21% at 21:00 UTC and peaks at 26% and 25% across the first two hours of live quoting before easing through 23%, 22%, 21% and 20% and returning to 19% and green at 04:00 UTC Monday, settling at 16-17% through the European morning. Forecast status is yellow at 21:00 UTC, orange at 22:00 and 23:00 UTC, then yellow through 03:00 UTC Monday and green thereafter.

That orange is conditional risk about the reopen, not an assertion that a one-way path has been observed. The reasoning is mechanical: a full weekend of unpriced Gaza, Lebanon and Hormuz headlines, plus a US sanctions package signposted for the coming week, has to clear into a single restart in thin liquidity, against a market whose implied volatility closed near the bottom of its 52-week range. The peak comes down one point from last hour because the marginal news was de-escalatory and because the sanctions package is now better bounded. If the gap is small and mean-reverting within the first hour, these forecast numbers will prove too high and the next assessments should say so plainly.

Stress rises from 80% to a peak of 87% at the restart, then decays to 74% by 11:00 UTC Monday as the weekend stack is absorbed, ticking back to 75% for the slots containing the 12:30 UTC Empire State release. Confidence eases to 76-78% through the last hours of the halt as Friday's evidence ages, then rises sharply to 84-87% once live quoting restores the price path that is the single missing input. dominantMode is mixed throughout except for event/whipsaw across the four hours spanning the restart.

No unambiguously high-impact scheduled US macro release falls inside this window - Empire State at 12:30 UTC Monday sits in the final slots and the ADP weekly print, housing starts, FOMC Minutes, jobless claims and flash PMIs are Tuesday through Friday. The restart itself is therefore the only genuine checkpoint in the forecast. The unscheduled Iran sanctions announcement is the wildcard: it has no timestamp, which is why it is reflected in the Stress path rather than in a second danger window.

Stress holds at 80%: the weekend stack is no longer growing, but it is also not yet priced, and Friday closed with VIX at 14.25, near the bottom of its 52-week range.

Sunday afternoon in Europe, five hours out. Tail drifts to 17% purely as time-to-restart compression, not as observed structure. Stress ticks to 81% because each further hour without a venue leaves the same unpriced headline stack facing a shorter runway into a single thin-liquidity reopen.

Four hours to restart. The Bessent sanctions package is still signposted for the coming week without a timestamp, which is why it sits in the Stress path rather than in a second danger window. Confidence eases to 77% as Friday's price evidence ages.

Roughly three hours out. Tail 18% remains comfortably low band and EA_ON: the contract requires observed directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks and repeated extension before Tail belongs above 25%, and none of those can be observed during a scheduled halt.

Two hours to the restart and the last quiet slot before the danger window opens at 21:55 UTC. Stress 83% carries the weight of a full weekend of Gaza, Lebanon and Hormuz flow plus an untimed US sanctions package, all of which has to clear into one reopen - though a working Kushner-Hamas-Egypt-Qatar channel is now a genuine offset on the other side of that ledger.
